methods.label: Express the tangent using one side length
methods.explanation:
Let \(t=CA>0\), and let \(\theta=\angle BAD\). Expressing both \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\) using the same side lengths will let those lengths cancel in their ratio.

Since \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), we have \(BD=CD=2\). Write \(p=AB\) and \(q=AD\). Applying the law of cosines at the given \(60^\circ\) angle gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
p^2&=t^2+16-4t,\\
q^2&=t^2+4-2t.
\end{aligned}
\]
Now apply the law of cosines in triangle \(BAD\), whose side opposite \(\theta\) has length \(2\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
pq\cos\theta
&=\frac{p^2+q^2-4}{2}\\
&=t^2-3t+8.
\end{aligned}
\]
This quantity is positive, since
\[
t^2-3t+8
=\left(t-\frac32\right)^2+\frac{23}{4}>0.
\]
Thus \(\theta\) is acute, and its tangent is defined.

The altitude from \(A\) to line \(BC\) has length \(t\sin60^\circ=\sqrt3t/2\). Using base \(BD=2\), the area of triangle \(BAD\) is \(\sqrt3t/2\). Using its sides \(p,q\) and included angle \(\theta\), that same area is \(pq\sin\theta/2\). Therefore
\[
pq\sin\theta=\sqrt3t.
\]
Taking the ratio gives
\[
\tan\theta
=\frac{\sqrt3t}{t^2-3t+8}
=\frac{\sqrt3}{t+8/t-3}.
\]
All divisions are valid because \(p,q,t>0\) and the cosine numerator above is positive.

For the positive numbers \(t\) and \(8/t\), AM-GM gives
\[
t+\frac8t\ge2\sqrt8=4\sqrt2,
\]
with equality exactly when \(t=8/t\), or \(t=2\sqrt2\). Hence
\[
\tan\theta\le
\frac{\sqrt3}{4\sqrt2-3}.
\]
The equality value \(CA=2\sqrt2\) gives a nondegenerate triangle with \(BC=4\) and \(\angle C=60^\circ\), so the bound is attained. The largest value is \(\boxed{\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4\sqrt2-3}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
